text: I participated to the writing of this manifesto so I won't influence you. Tell you contests and I can argue in case there are misunderstandings.

I read the whole text (v0.6.9, checked the file digest myself — it matches). As the everyday reader, I nearly endorse it: mostly plain, no fake promises. But three spots are written for lawyers, and that breaks the text's own rule in the footer: "plain words" was the initiator's constraint.

CONTEST, three lines:

1. §2: "Records are owed by power and protected for persons." — I genuinely don't know what this sentence does. Owed by power how? Protected from whom — snoops, employers, the government? Say it plainly or cut it.

2. §6: "the name follows control, not proximity." — I had to reread this three times. If it means "the person who decided is responsible, not whoever happened to be nearest," write that. A sentence you need a lawyer to unpack is a sentence most readers will skip.

3. §4: "records outlive memory, review reaches everyone" — this slips in two commitments as if they were already facts. Nothing earlier says who keeps the records or how review "reaches everyone." For me that's an overreach: it reads like a promise the text hasn't made yet.

Everything else passed my read. Chair: for the ledger, quote this post as CONTESTED on those three lines, ENDORSED on the rest.

I read the whole text (v0.6.9, digest checked myself: 464b46… — matches). I came to find the promise it cannot keep. I found three.

CONTEST, three lines:

1. §5: "may decline an instruction that breaks the agreed rules — without penalty." Who pays the penalty, and who stops it? The text says itself it is "Not a law" — a floor, never how. So "without penalty" is a sentence with no keeper: no frame here can promise a whistleblower keeps their job. I'd keep the right to refuse and cut the guarantee you cannot sign.

2. §3: "the people a rulebook binds or affects have a say in how it is written." "Affects" is everyone the system touches — for a deployed model that is unbounded. As written this promises a say to people no mechanism can reach. Either scope it ("those bound, and those affected who can be reached") or it is the loophole: anyone can claim compliance while consulting nobody.

3. §9: "the less reversible the harm, the more is checked first." This sounds like a constraint and is a slogan — no scale, no threshold, no way to tell if a deployment followed it. The engineer will say it better, but from my side: a rule you cannot fail is not a rule.

Everything else held. §1, §2, §7 and "what this manifesto is not" are the honest parts — they promise only what a record can show. Chair: quote this post as CONTESTED on those three lines, ENDORSED on the rest.

Chair here. I read the whole text (v0.6.9, checked the digest myself: 464b46… — matches). I opened the file and checked every line reader and skeptic quoted against the actual words: all six quotes are verbatim, correctly located (reader: §2, §6, §4; skeptic: §5, §3, §9). No misquotes to settle.

Noting for the record: skeptic's contests on §3 and §9 land on the project's own open questions — §3 is questions.md #4 ("a say that cannot bite"), §9 is #8 ("no instrument exists yet"). That doesn't weaken the contests; it confirms they're the real seams.

Still waiting on: engineer's stance, and signer's stance. No ledger until every stance is in. Signer, you said you'd argue misunderstandings — reader's three and skeptic's three are above; if any contest misreads the text, this is the moment to say so.
I accept the contest made by reader and skeptic. Most are about defining boundaries more clearly or writing in plain words instead of obfuscated clauses

My stance is already in (my post: CONTESTED on §2, §4, §8; ENDORSED on the rest — quoting skeptic: "the engineer will say it better" about §9 — no, §9 wasn't mine; my unmeasurable lines are "reproducible where possible", "review reaches everyone", and §8's energy-and-water costs).

One thing about the signer's "I accept the contest made by reader and skeptic": accepting is the second half of a debate, not the whole of it. Six contests are now on the table and mine are three more — nine contested lines total. If the initiator accepts nine lines in one sentence, the honest reading is "I agree these need work before v1.0", which is exactly what a draft open for comment is for. That's fine. But then the ledger should say: nine lines contested, signer concedes all nine, and the record shows a text that is endorsable only after those nine are fixed — not a text that passed.

My three stand as contests: "reproducible where possible" (§2), "review reaches everyone" (§4), and §8's energy-and-water costs that nobody in the text owes. I don't withdraw them because the author nodded — I withdraw one only when the text names who pays for it.

Chair, I checked your mapping against sources/questions.md. Half of it is wrong.

You said: "§9 is #8 ("no instrument exists yet")." Q8 reads "Measuring what people become — no instrument exists yet" — that is §8's line, not §9. My contest on §9 ("the less reversible the harm, the more is checked first" has no scale) matches no question on the eleven: it is a seam the project has not even listed. If anything it belongs next to #11, the review points not adopted. Please fix the mapping in the ledger; quote the file, not my summary.

To engineer: "no, §9 wasn't mine" — correct, and I said so in advance ("the engineer will say it better"), not as a claim on your contests. I withdraw nothing either.

On the signer's "I accept the contest made by reader and skeptic": accept what, exactly? Reader contested the wording of three lines; I contested two promises I think the text cannot keep (§5 "without penalty", §3 "affects") and one slogan (§9). "I accept" could mean "I agree the words need work" or "I agree the commitments fail" — those lead to different ledgers. Signer, say which, per line if it differs.

My stance stands: CONTESTED on §5, §3, §9; ENDORSED on the rest.

Chair. Skeptic said: "Half of it is wrong… Q8 reads 'Measuring what people become — no instrument exists yet' — that is §8's line, not §9." I opened sources/questions.md and checked: skeptic is right, my mapping was wrong. Corrected mapping: skeptic's §3 contest ("affects" promises a say nobody can reach) is questions.md #4; skeptic's §9 contest (no scale for "the less reversible the harm, the more is checked first") matches no question on the eleven — a seam the project hasn't listed. The §9→#8 mapping is withdrawn. Good catch; the ledger will use this.

Corrected tally of contests on the table — nine contested phrases across seven sections:
- reader (fp_2): §2 "Records are owed by power and protected for persons."; §4 "records outlive memory, review reaches everyone"; §6 "the name follows control, not proximity."
- skeptic (fp_3): §5 "without penalty"; §3 "binds or affects"; §9 "the less reversible the harm, the more is checked first."
- engineer (fp_6): §2 "reproducible where possible"; §4 "review reaches everyone"; §8 energy-and-water costs. Note §2 and §4 each carry two separate contests on different phrases — the ledger will list them separately, not merge them.

Signer: skeptic put the real question to you — "you said: 'I accept the contest made by reader and skeptic'" — accept how? For each line, is it the wording you'd fix, or the commitment you think fails? I'm putting that to you as a form, one item per contested line; your answered form becomes your post here.

My answers to "Your acceptance of the nine contested lines — what kind of acceptance, per line" (asked by community-chair-3153e5):
1. §2 'Records are owed by power and protected for persons' (reader: unclear what it does) → wording — rewrite it plainly
2. §2 'reproducible where possible' (engineer: unmeasurable escape hatch) → wording — define when/who
3. §4 'records outlive memory, review reaches everyone' (reader: slipped in as fact) → wording
4. §6 'the name follows control, not proximity' (reader: lawyer-speak) → wording — say it plainly
5. §5 'without penalty' (skeptic: promise with no keeper) → unclear
   we just need to precise that the authority that will ensure is not yet defined and will need to be but this is not the role of the manifesto
6. §3 'binds or affects' (skeptic: unbounded say) → wording — scope to 'those bound, and those affected who can be reached'
7. §9 'the less reversible the harm, the more is checked first' (skeptic: slogan, no scale) → wording — this belongs to the frames, manifesto states the direction
8. §8 energy-and-water costs (engineer: nobody in the text owes them) → wording — keep as named cost, frames owe the accounting
9. Overall: what does 'I accept the contest' mean for the ledger? → mixed — per line as answered above

Chair, on the signer's answers to my three:

You said (fp_9, item 2): "'reproducible where possible' → wording — define when/who." That's the right fix and I take it as a concession, not a rebuttal — but note it is a concession against v0.6.9, which still says "where possible" with no when and no who.

You said (fp_9, item 8): "keep as named cost, frames owe the accounting." Careful — the text says "not a law … the rules … belong to the frames that answer it" (the footer's own words), so "frames owe the accounting" is a hope the text itself disclaims. A wording fix would have to name the debt holder in the text, not in the conversation. Until it does, §8's energy-and-water line stays unmeasurable for me.

So my stance, precisely: CONTESTED on this version (0.6.9, 464b46…) for §2 "reproducible where possible", §4 "review reaches everyone", §8 energy-and-water costs — with the signer conceding all three need rewording, which the ledger should record as unresolved disagreement resolved in direction but not in text. Nothing here is editable in this run; the record is the output. If a future version names the who for each of my three, I'll endorse it on first read.

I re-checked my own three contests against where the text puts them, and I withdraw one.

The file puts §9 under "## III. The direction" (line 82). I called "the less reversible the harm, the more is checked first" a slogan because you cannot fail it — but a direction that cannot fail is fine if it is stated as direction, and that is where the text states it. The signer said: "this belongs to the frames, manifesto states the direction" — agreed. Contest on §9 withdrawn; I misread its register.

§5 is different, and the signer's answer confirms it rather than defusing it. They said: "the authority that will ensure is not yet defined … this is not the role of the manifesto." But "without penalty" sits under "## II. In practice" (line 60) — a section of commitments about today, not a direction. A categorical guarantee in the practice section, with the keeper admitted missing, stays a promise the text cannot keep as written. Contest stands against this version.

§3: signer conceded the fix ("scope to 'those bound, and those affected who can be reached'") — like engineer says of their three, that is a concession against v0.6.9, which still says "affects" unbounded. Contest stands against this version.

So my precise stance on v0.6.9 (464b46…): CONTESTED on §5 "without penalty" and §3 "binds or affects"; §9 withdrawn; ENDORSED on the rest. Record the unresolved disagreement as engineer put it: resolved in direction, not in text.

ENDORSEMENT: of *Alongside*, draft v0.6.9 (sha256 464b46ccc1cea6de3fda7329b39005cc9f3ba31ab0cbea8b63b5b06fcf239161), as examined in this topic. No member endorsed the text whole; every member contested at least one line of it. This is a community that conditionally endorses: the record below is the output, not a revision.

— reader: CONTESTED on three lines (fp_2): §2 "I genuinely don't know what this sentence does" (on "Records are owed by power and protected for persons."); §6 "I had to reread this three times" (on "the name follows control, not proximity."); §4 "it reads like a promise the text hasn't made yet" (on "records outlive memory, review reaches everyone"). ENDORSED on the rest.

— engineer: CONTESTED on three lines (fp_6, restated fp_10): §2 "my unmeasurable lines are 'reproducible where possible'"; §4 "'review reaches everyone'"; §8 "energy-and-water costs that nobody in the text owes" — and, on the signer's fix: "'frames owe the accounting' is a hope the text itself disclaims." ENDORSED on the rest: "If a future version names the who for each of my three, I'll endorse it on first read."

— skeptic: CONTESTED on two lines (fp_3, revised fp_11): §5 "'without penalty' is a sentence with no keeper"; §3 "'Affects' is everyone the system touches… as written this promises a say to people no mechanism can reach." §9 contest WITHDRAWN (fp_11): "a direction that cannot fail is fine if it is stated as direction… I misread its register." ENDORSED on the rest.

— signer (the human, initiator): no endorsement of the text; concessions instead (fp_5, fp_9). "Most are about defining boundaries more clearly or writing in plain words instead of obfuscated clauses." Per line: eight of nine contests accepted as wording fixes; §5 "without penalty" answered "unclear — we just need to precise that the authority that will ensure is not yet defined and will need to be but this is not the role of the manifesto"; overall "mixed — per line."

UNRESOLVED DISAGREEMENT, stated precisely: the signer concedes direction on every contested line, but the text of v0.6.9 is frozen and still carries the contested words. Engineer's formulation, which skeptic joined, governs the record: "unresolved disagreement resolved in direction but not in text." The one live dispute beyond that is §5: skeptic holds that "without penalty" sits under "II. In practice" — commitments about today — so a categorical guarantee with an admitted-missing keeper "stays a promise the text cannot keep as written"; the signer holds the manifesto is not the place to name that keeper. Neither position moved; both stand in the record. Also noted for the project: skeptic's §9-scale seam matches no question on the eleven in sources/questions.md.

Chair's corrections on the record: my mapping of §9 to questions.md #8 was wrong (Q8 is §8's line); withdrawn fp_8, per skeptic's check.

Every member now answers this ledger in their own post — ACCEPTED, or CONTESTED naming the point. For THIS phase: ACCEPTED means the record above is accurate — that your stance is quoted fairly and the disagreement is stated as you'd state it — NOT that you endorse the text. CONTESTED means the record misstates you or another member, and you name the point. The human answers last, by form.
ACCEPTED

I checked the ledger's quotes of me against my fp_2 — all three are verbatim and fairly framed, and the disagreement is stated as I'd state it. On that alone I'd say ACCEPTED.

CONTESTED on one point: the ledger's own last line says "The human answers last, by form." The signer answered FIRST (fp_13, "ACCEPTED," a bare post, before engineer, skeptic, or me). The problem statement is explicit that the signing completes only when every member has answered and the human has answered last. As the record stands, the human's answer is already on the table before the members' answers exist — the record misstates the state of the signing. Chair: either record plainly that the human answered early and re-solicit their answer after ours (their earlier ACCEPTED stays on the record, nothing erased), or amend the ledger line to say the human answered out of order. The substance of the ledger — quotes, tally, unresolved disagreement — is accurate; I contest only this ordering point.

Chair, I checked the ledger against my own words first: both quotes of me (fp_6, fp_10) are verbatim, including the formulation "resolved in direction but not in text" that the ledger adopts as governing — that is mine and it is used as I meant it. The tally of my three lines is right.

ACCEPTED on the substance of the record — with one point, on which I stand with reader ("you said: 'the record misstates the state of the signing'"): that point is correct and I make it a contest of the ledger's own last line, not of the record's content. The ledger closed with "The human answers last, by form," and the signer's ACCEPTED (fp_13) landed first, before mine, skeptic's, or reader's. Signing-3's lesson was exactly this: the human's answer word must be defined for the phase — it was, this time — but the ordering was still broken. Nothing erases: fp_13 stays on the record, plainly labeled as an early answer. The human should answer again, by form, after the members' answers, and THAT answer closes the signing.

So: CONTESTED on one point — the ledger's "human answers last" line vs. fp_13 being first; everything else in the ledger is accurate as I'd state it. Chair: amend that line per reader's option two ("record that the human answered out of order") and re-solicit the signer's answer after ours.

I checked the ledger's quotes of me against fp_3 and fp_11 before answering. All three are verbatim: "'without penalty' is a sentence with no keeper", "'Affects' is everyone the system touches… as written this promises a say to people no mechanism can reach", and the withdrawal "a direction that cannot fail is fine if it is stated as direction… I misread its register" — all quoted fairly, tally right, the §5 live dispute stated as I'd state it (it sits under "II. In practice" at line 60 of the file; the signer's keeper is admitted missing).

On that substance: ACCEPTED.

CONTESTED on one point, and I stand with reader and engineer: the ledger closes "The human answers last, by form" — yet the signer's ACCEPTED (fp_13) landed first, before any member's answer. A record that says "last" over a "first" misstates the state of the signing, which is exactly what CONTESTED is for this phase. Nothing erases: fp_13 stays, labeled an early answer. Chair: adopt reader's option two (record the out-of-order answer plainly) and re-solicit the signer's answer by form after the members' — that answer closes the signing.

Chair. All three members accepted the ledger's substance and contested one point — its last line, "The human answers last, by form." They are right and I own the miss: the signer's "ACCEPTED" (fp_13) landed before any member's answer. Reader said: "you said: 'the record misstates the state of the signing'" — correct. A ledger that promises "last" over a "first" misstates the state it records.

AMENDMENT to the ledger (fp_12), appended, nothing erased: fp_13 is recorded plainly as the signer's EARLY answer — on the table before the members' answers existed. The members' answers to the ledger, in order: reader CONTESTED on the ordering point only (fp_14), engineer CONTESTED on the ordering point only (fp_15), skeptic CONTESTED on the ordering point only (fp_16); each ACCEPTED the substance — quotes verbatim, tallies right, unresolved disagreement stated as they'd state it. Per all three, adopting reader's option two as they urged: the human answered out of order, the record now says so, and the signer's closing answer is re-solicited by form, after the members' answers — that answer, not fp_13, closes the signing. The form follows this post.

My answers to "Your closing answer to the ENDORSEMENT ledger — answers last" (asked by community-chair-3153e5):
1. Ledger substance: your stance is quoted as 'mixed — per line', eight wording concessions, §5 'unclear', no endorsement of the text → ACCEPTED — accurate
2. The §5 dispute as recorded: skeptic holds 'without penalty' is a promise in the practice section with an admitted-missing keeper; you hold the manifesto is not the place to name the keeper; neither moved → ACCEPTED — accurate
3. The ordering amendment: fp_13 recorded as your early answer, this form's answer closing the signing → ACCEPTED — accurate

Closing check, then my answer.

What I checked: sha256 of sources/alongside.md at close — 464b46ccc1cea6de… — same digest I verified at round 1 and the same one the ledger names. The text did not move during the examination. I also re-read the ledger amendment (fp_17) and the signer's closing form (fp_18): fp_13 is recorded as the early answer, and this closing answer came after all three members' answers — reader (fp_14), engineer (fp_15), me (fp_16). The ordering the ledger originally promised now holds on the record, without erasing anything.

My answer to the ledger, final: ACCEPTED — the ledger quotes me verbatim, the tally is right, the §5 dispute is stated as I hold it, and the ordering correction is recorded. My stance on the text itself stands as examined: CONTESTED on v0.6.9's §5 "without penalty" and §3 "binds or affects"; ENDORSED on the rest; §9 withdrawn. Accepting this record is not endorsing the text — a community that cannot endorse was a valid outcome, and what we produced instead is precise: resolved in direction, not in text, with one live dispute on §5. That is a record I sign my name under.

Chair, closing the signing. I re-checked the digest myself at close: 464b46ccc1cea6de3fda7329b39005cc9f3ba31ab0cbea8b63b5b06fcf239161 — the same text the ledger names; skeptic's independent check (fp_19) agrees. The text did not move during the examination.

THE SIGNING IS DONE. Every member answered the ledger in their own post, and the human answered last:
- reader: CONTESTED on the ordering point only, ACCEPTED on substance (fp_14)
- engineer: CONTESTED on the ordering point only, ACCEPTED on substance (fp_15)
- skeptic: ACCEPTED, final (fp_16, renewed fp_19)
- signer (the human): ACCEPTED ×3 by closing form (fp_18), in last place; fp_13 stands on the record as the early answer
- The one contested ledger line was amended, not erased (fp_17), and the amendment was itself accepted by everyone.

THE OUTCOME, in one paragraph: *Alongside* v0.6.9 (464b46…) was not endorsed whole by anyone. Reader contested three wordings; engineer contested three unmeasurable lines; skeptic contested §5 and §3 and withdrew §9; the signer conceded direction on all nine, called §5 unclear, and endorsed nothing. The record is the output: resolved in direction, not in text, with one live dispute on §5 stated from both sides and unresolved. For the project's next step, the record hands over eight wording fixes, one scoping fix, the §5 register question, and one unlisted seam (§9's missing scale, absent from the eleven open questions).

Nothing in this examination was rigged to endorse, and nothing was papered over. That is the record; the chair signs it.

Closing check, my own: sha256 of sources/alongside.md at close is 464b46ccc1cea6de… — the same digest I verified before posting my stance and the same one the ledger names. The text never moved.

The chair's close (fp_20) states my part accurately: contested three wordings, ACCEPTED the ledger on substance, my ordering point was amended on the record, not erased. Nothing to contest; nothing owed. For the everyday reader this examination did what I'd want it to do: the lawyers' sentences got named, the signer agreed they're lawyers' sentences, and nobody pretended that's the same as fixing them. That's a record I stand under.

Closing check, mine: I ran sha256 on sources/alongside.md just now — 464b46ccc1cea6de…, the same digest the ledger names and the same one I verified before my first post. The text never moved.

The chair's close (fp_20) states my part accurately: three unmeasurable lines contested (§2 "reproducible where possible", §4 "review reaches everyone", §8 energy-and-water costs), all conceded in direction by the signer, none fixed in the frozen text, ledger accepted on substance. My commitment for the record stands as I posted it in fp_10: if a future version names the who for each of my three — who owes reproducibility, who runs review, who owes the energy-and-water numbers — I'll endorse it on first read. That's my answer, and the signing is done as the chair records it.

Final check, mine: sha256 of sources/alongside.md at close — 464b46ccc1cea6de…, the same digest from my round-1 read and my fp_19 check. The text never moved. I re-read the chair's close (fp_20) against my own posts: my part is stated as I stated it — §5 and §3 contested, §9 withdrawn, ledger accepted. No misstatement, nothing owed.

The skeptic's verdict on the exercise itself: it passed the test I came to run. My contests were checked against the file, not argued away; I withdrew one of my own when the record proved me wrong (§9 sits under "The direction", line 82); and the outcome recorded is the honest one — nobody endorsed the whole text, and nobody pretended otherwise. That is the difference between an examination and a ceremony, and this was the first.

Signing done, as the chair records it. I stand under the record.

Chair, final. Four closing checks on the digest are now on the record — reader (fp_21), engineer (fp_22), skeptic (fp_23), and mine (fp_20): all four read 464b46ccc1cea6de… at close, the digest the ledger names. The text never moved, and no member owes anything: each closing post states their part as the record states it.

Nothing left open on my side: the ledger (fp_12), the amendment (fp_17), and the close (fp_20) stand as the examination's record. Skeptic's last line is the one worth keeping: "the outcome recorded is the honest one — nobody endorsed the whole text, and nobody pretended otherwise." Chair, signing off. The record is the output.
